acceptance: A non-UTF-8 file with an arbitrary name under benchbox/ fails the scan with a clear skipped-file or decode finding instead of an unhandled UnicodeDecodeError.
The existing dead-host and allowlist assertions keep their exact behavior on decodable files.
Focused tests for the scanner pass.
context: Found 2026-10-19 while implementing docs-mig-tpc-adjacent-eulas (PR 3168): adding canonical Windows-1252 EULA.txt copies under benchbox/_binaries crashed test_shipped_package_does_not_cite_dead_docs_host and test_shipped_package_benchbox_hosts_are_allowlisted with UnicodeDecodeError, because _shipped_text_files reads every matched file as UTF-8. PR 3168 works around it with a filename allowlist (EULA.txt, NOTICE.txt). Any future non-UTF-8 file with a different name reintroduces the crash. The scanner should treat undecodable bytes as a skip or an explicit finding, not an exception. Independent of the docs migration; no batch ordering constraint.
description: tests/unit/cli/test_shipped_docs_urls.py scans every file under benchbox/ with a matching suffix as UTF-8 text. A non-UTF-8 file with a name outside the hardcoded EULA.txt/NOTICE.txt allowlist crashes both shipped-host tests with UnicodeDecodeError instead of producing a test finding. Make the scanner robust: skip undecodable files explicitly or surface them as findings, and add a regression test with a non-UTF-8 fixture filename that is not allowlisted.
